screen: Demo mode step 3 'Overview: radar time-lapse' (and step 4)
what: Step 3 of the demo, the radar step, opens with the radar overlay switched off. The demo passes the hint `view=radar`, but Overview only reads `radar=1`, so the step shows plain pipes and no radar. At 1280x720 the 'Show radar overlay' checkbox and the date slider sit below the fold of the side panel, so the presenter has to scroll the panel to find them. That breaks the 'one click per step' rule and the pitch's radar-image moment. Steps 3 and 4 render the same screen.
evidence: src/features/story/pitch.ts:54 `query: { view: "radar" }` and :67 `query: { view: "pipes" }`; src/screens/Overview.tsx:43 `on: query.get("radar") === "1"` (no 'view' key read anywhere). Playwright demo walk: checkbox state on step 3 = [false, true] (overlay unchecked) in demo_1280x720_en.json and demo_1440x900_ar.json. Screenshot docs/qa/shots/verify-ux/demo_1280x720_en_step03.png: no radar, NISAR radar section cut off below the panel.
fix: In pitch.ts set step 3 to `query: { radar: "1", date: "2026-09-16" }` and step 4 to `query: { radar: "0" }`. Alternatively make Overview accept `view==="radar"`. Overview reads the query only in a useState initialiser, and EmbeddedScreen is keyed by step.screen, so steps 3 and 4 share one instance. Key EmbeddedScreen by step.id (`key={step.id}`), or add an effect that syncs `rs.on` from the query. When embedded, also scroll the side panel so the NISAR radar block is in view.

screen: Demo mode steps 6 (Twin), 7 (Records), 9 (Impact) at 1280x720; step 6 also at 1440x900
what: The numbers the presenter says on these steps are below the fold of the demo stage. Twin: the '1 other junction' value is cut off at 1280x720, and '788 of 850' is off-screen at both 1280x720 and 1440x900. Records: only 'Doubt left' is visible; the Gap A–E probability bars and the 'Why AI' figures (46.9% vs 26.7%) are not, so a judge pressing 'AI: place next logger' cannot see the bars move. Impact: 86.4 m³/day, 31,536 m³/year and '2 sites vs 1,287 km' are below the fold. The pitch rule is that every number spoken is on screen at that moment.
evidence: docs/qa/shots/verify-ux/demo_1280x720_en_step06.png (big '1' clipped at the panel bottom, no 788), demo_1440x900_ar_step06.png (788 card cut off), demo_1280x720_en_step07.png (no gap bars), demo_1280x720_en_step09.png. Stage scroll heights from the demo JSON: impact 1820/534, sources 2593/554.
fix: Use the `embedded` prop, which Twin ignores and Records only turns into an unstyled `is-embedded` class. When embedded: hide the kicker and intro paragraph and collapse 'More scenarios'. Render the 'Junctions dropping more than 1 m' comparison card (leak 1 vs main break 788 of 850) directly under the scenario buttons. In Records put the gap bars right under the action row, so `.hf-screen.is-embedded` needs real CSS. For Impact, move the 'One hidden leak' and 'Crew effort' cards to the first row, or add a `focus` query that scrolls to them.

what: The token count never appears. Impact reads `localStorage['mb.triage.usage' | 'mb.triage.last' | 'mb.triage']`, but nothing in the app writes those keys, so the card always says 'Run AI triage to see the token count of one run.', even right after a live triage run. The recorded run also has `usage: null`. The spec asks for the per-run token count from the triage response, and the pitch's answer to the business judge says 'the screen shows the token count'.
evidence: `grep -rn "mb\.triage" src` finds only src/features/story/usage.ts, the reader; there is no writer. server/recorded/triage.json:162 `"usage": null`. Screenshot tall_1440_ar_impact.png: the card shows the 'run triage' prompt.
fix: In useTriageStream (or Triage.tsx when the final event arrives), add `localStorage.setItem('mb.triage.usage', JSON.stringify({input_tokens, output_tokens, source, model, at}))` whenever `usage` is present. Do one live run on the demo laptop now, and save its real usage into server/recorded/triage.json under the 'Recorded run' label, so the offline fallback also shows a sourced token count.

what: A fresh clone running `npm run fetch:pipes` does not reproduce the demo data. The total is 1,291 km instead of the 1,287 km in the README and pitch, because the script uses an equirectangular length. source_handle is null (it reads EntityHandle; the real field is Handle). 929 pipe_ids beyond about KRK-07474 map to different CAD layers, because paging has no orderByFields. The ids tied to the wet spots (KRK-02550, 05463, 02449, 00833) do match.
evidence: Ran scripts/fetch_pipes.ts into a scratch folder and compared with data/pipes/karak_pipes.geojson. Same 8,778 features; km by class 359.8/395.6/321.9/169.7/44.2 vs 358.6/394.2/320.6/169.1/44.0; 929 layer mismatches by pipe_id. ArcGIS field list shows `Handle`. scripts/fetch_pipes.ts:39-46 (length) and the query URL in main().
fix: Add &orderByFields=OBJECTID to the query, read f.properties.Handle, and compute geodesic length with a haversine, so a fresh clone shows the same 1,287 km and the same pipe ids.

what: The README says "Needs Node 20+", but server/index.ts:30 calls process.loadEnvFile(), which needs Node 20.12+ or 21.7+. On an earlier Node 20 the call throws inside the try/catch, the key in .env is silently ignored, and the UI tells the user "Why recorded: No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on this machine", which is the wrong reason.
evidence: README.md:15; package.json engines ">=20"; server/index.ts:29-33 (try { process.loadEnvFile() } catch {}).
fix: Say "Node 20.12+" in the README and set engines to ">=20.12". Or log a warning when process.loadEnvFile is missing and report that in the recorded-run reason.

what: The README gives two different numbers for the same test (Bayesian, 10 loggers, all 5 gaps right, 1,440 cases): 46.1% (MLP 37.2%) from hydrofingerprint_results.json and 46.9% (MLP 46.2%) from hydrofingerprint_robustness.json. Nothing explains the gap; a judge reading the table will see an inconsistency. The app quotes only 46.9%.
evidence: README.md:168 and README.md:169. data/hydrofingerprint/hydrofingerprint_robustness.json nominal_test.bayes_all5 = 46.9, mlp_all5 = 46.2.
fix: Quote one run, or add a short note: "two training runs: hf_train.py (46.1%) and the hf_baseline.py/hf_robust.py re-run (46.9%); the app shows the latter".
